blocks.text: Lots and land in Salmon River

items.t: Valley-floor parcels: farm and acreage houses on large rural lots along the river valley, under the Township Rural Plan designations and Zoning Bylaw No. 2500; the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2.
Upland parcels (56 Avenue / Rawlison Crescent side): the same fee-simple acreage form on the upland side of the district — horse owners using the upland lots are part of the typical-buyer picture.
Strata or freehold: most Salmon River properties are freehold acreages with no strata. Where there is a strata, BC's Strata Property Act applies.
ALR vs non-ALR split: farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; no percentage split is available. Confirm a specific parcel on the ALC maps.

Water and sewer: rural properties here may use wells and septic. Look up a property's well in GWELLS, the provincial database of registered wells and aquifers; well reports are due within 90 days of building, changing or decommissioning a well. Unless the Township confirms a property is on city services, plan on checking the well and septic.

Flood character of the land itself: the Salmon River valley is Fraser River floodplain land — the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station was originally built to help mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet, provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise, and has flood box gates that close as river levels rise. Valley-floor land value is inseparable from that system.
Riparian character: the Salmon River is salmon-bearing, so setbacks and riparian rules can limit building envelopes near the river. Price buildable area, not gross area.
Salmon River Ranch

Market figures: in September 2026, 22 detached homes were listed in Salmon River and 5 sold (23%, one of the stronger rates in rural Langley, though from few listings), and 4 condos and townhomes were listed with none sold. The board doesn't publish medians for Salmon River; the Langley-wide medians were $1,345,000 for detached homes and $611,000 for condos and townhomes. It also doesn't publish land prices.

blocks.text: Where lots come up and what to know

items.t: Municipality: Township of Langley, BC — Salmon River is the rural district along the Salmon River in the township's northwest, north of the Otter area and south of Fort Langley.
On MLS®, the Fraser Valley Real Estate Board calls the area "Salmon River".

The area follows the Salmon River valley between 232 Street and 264 Street, from the Fraser River side south toward 40 Avenue, with Rawlison Crescent and 56 Avenue on the upland side. The Township doesn't publish a boundary for it.
The name is the river's name: the Salmon River is a salmon-bearing watercourse, and Metro Vancouver watershed material covers the Salmon River watershed.
Nearby areas: Fort Langley to the north, Otter District to the south, Walnut Grove to the west, Aldergrove to the southeast.

Main roads and commute: 56 Avenue and Rawlison Crescent on the upland, 232 Street and 240 Street as the north–south edges, and River Road / Glover Road toward Fort Langley; Highway 1 access is south via the 200 Street or 232 Street interchanges; there is no SkyTrain or West Coast Express station in the district.

Transit: route 562 (Walnut Grove / Langley Centre) runs on Glover Road via 96 Avenue, 88 Avenue and 202 Street to Carvolth Exchange, serving the Fort Langley edge of the area. I don't know of any bus route on 56 Avenue, Rawlison Crescent or the valley roads.

Schools (SD35 Langley): catchments go by address, so check the specific address with the school district. Coghlan Fundamental Elementary, 4452 256 Street, a district school of choice, is on the upland east side. There's no school in the Salmon River valley itself.

Parks and facilities: the Salmon River Natural Area is a Township park in the Fort Langley area. There's no recreation centre or library in the area; the nearest Township facilities are in Fort Langley and Walnut Grove.
Compact R-CL lots, where that zone applies, are 220 m² to 464.5 m² under Zoning Bylaw 2500. That zone and the Willoughby plan are for Willoughby, not Salmon River.

The pump station is the valley's defining infrastructure: the Salmon River Pump Station has flood box gates that close as Fraser River levels rise, and Council has authorized detailed design and tendering for its upgrades — a live Township project a valley-floor buyer should read before valuing land inside the dykes.
The nearest school isn't always the catchment school, so check the address with the Langley School District. There's no school in the valley itself.

Health care is outside the area: Langley Memorial Hospital, 22051 Fraser Highway, to the southwest, has a 24-hour emergency department, and the Langley Urgent and Primary Care Centre is at 202-20434 64 Avenue. There's no hospital or clinic in the area.

Listings tagged Salmon River can include Langley City condos. A 1-bedroom condo at "Cornerstone North by Marcon" near Kwantlen Polytechnic University is labelled "Salmon River" in the listing feed, but it is Langley City product, not Salmon River land, and shouldn't be compared with acreages.

items.t: The usual duplex form: Rural land sits under Zoning Bylaw No. 2500 (the district's farm and acreage homes sit in the rural zones, including RU-2).

blocks.text: Where duplexes come up and what to know

items.t: ALR and flooding: some farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve, so check a specific property on the Agricultural Land Commission's map. On ALR land, the main house can be up to 500 m², a suite must be entirely inside it, and one additional home is allowed without an application, up to 90 m² on properties of 40 ha or less or 186 m² on larger ones, subject to Township bylaws. The valley is on the Fraser River floodplain. The Township says the Salmon River Pump Station was built to help prevent flooding of the farmland during the spring freshet, and its flood gates close when the Fraser River rises. Council has approved design and tendering for upgrades to the station.

faq.q: What kind of land actually sells in Salmon River?
faq.a: Large fee-simple rural parcels — valley-floor farm land and 56 Avenue / Rawlison Crescent upland acreages — parcel by parcel.

faq.q: Is the land in the ALR?
faq.a: Farm land in the valley is in the Agricultural Land Reserve in places; confirm a specific parcel on the ALC ALR maps before assuming a farm use, a second dwelling or a subdivision is possible.

faq.q: Is the valley in a floodplain?
faq.a: Yes — the valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Salmon River Pump Station provides flood protection when Fraser River levels rise and was built to mitigate flooding of the surrounding agricultural lands during freshet.

faq.q: Can I subdivide a big parcel?
faq.a: Get the zone confirmed through the Township's GeoSource Map Schedules before writing on split potential.

faq.q: Is there a duplex development in Salmon River I can buy into?
faq.a: The homes are freehold acreages and rural houses with no strata, some with suites. Value a suite as a suite under the Township's 120 m² limit, not as half a duplex.

faq.q: Are Cedar Springs and Westfield Courts duplexes, or homes on land you own?
faq.a: No. Both are manufactured home parks where you rent the pad. A home there is a home on rented land, not a duplex.

faq.q: Is the Salmon River district in a floodplain?
faq.a: The valley is Fraser River floodplain land; the Township states the Pump Station provides flood protection when river levels rise, and upgrades are in detailed design and tendering.

faq.q: Which schools serve a Salmon River address?
faq.a: Check the exact address with the Langley School District before counting on a school; a result for one address doesn't apply to another. There's no school in the valley itself.
Route 562 runs on Glover Road at the Fort Langley edge of the area, between Langley Centre and Walnut Grove / Carvolth Exchange. I don't know of any route on the valley roads.

faq.q: Can an acreage add a second dwelling?
faq.a: On ALR land the ALC permits one additional residence without an ALC application where its size rules are met (up to 90 m² at 40 ha or less, up to 186 m² over 40 ha), subject to Township bylaws; the Township's small-scale multi-unit rules also allow a suite or accessory unit on lots over 4,050 m² depending on zoning.
